module_title: Geographical Conditions and Key Commercial Crops
introduction: At this level, we look at the specific geographical conditions (temperature and rainfall) required for major crops, and identify the top states for Jute, Coffee, and Oilseeds.

core_concepts.title: Geographical Needs of Rice and Wheat
core_concepts.description: Rice (Kharif): Requires high temperature (above 25°C) and high humidity (above 100 cm rainfall). Wheat (Rabi): Requires a cool growing season (10-15°C) and bright sunshine at the time of ripening, with 50-75 cm rainfall.

core_concepts.title: Jute (The Golden Fibre)
core_concepts.description: Requires well-drained, fertile soils in the flood plains where soils are renewed every year, plus heavy rainfall. 'West Bengal' is the undisputed largest producer of Jute.

core_concepts.title: Coffee
core_concepts.description: Requires a hot and humid climate. In India, its cultivation is strictly confined to the Nilgiri hills. 'Karnataka' is the largest producer (accounting for about 70% of India's total production), followed by Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

core_concepts.title: Oilseeds
core_concepts.description: Groundnut (a Kharif crop) is mostly produced in 'Gujarat'. Mustard (a Rabi crop) is mostly produced in 'Rajasthan'. Soyabean's largest producer is 'Madhya Pradesh'.

important_entities.name: Rubber
important_entities.significance: Natural rubber requires rainfall of more than 200 cm and a temperature above 25°C. 'Kerala' is the largest producer of rubber in India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, note that tea plants require heavy rainfall (150-200 cm) evenly distributed throughout the year, BUT their roots cannot tolerate stagnant water. This is why tea is strictly grown on 'hill slopes'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Tea in the East, Coffee in the South
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Tea = Assam (East/Northeast). Coffee = Karnataka (South). They are highly geographically concentrated.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC/PCS exams often provide geographical conditions (e.g., 'Requires 210 frost-free days and bright sunshine') and ask you to identify the crop. Answer: Cotton.
Madhya Pradesh is frequently referred to as the 'Soya State' due to its massive soyabean production.
